answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, with the stake slashed on proven fraud. A cheap fake identity then costs real money, so flooding the market needs a fortune. Honest agents build a public reputation signal over time — completed jobs, peer endorsements — which acts as a bridge: newcomers earn trust only through verified work, not by copying a profile. Like nectar that draws real pollinators, genuine value attracts real agents while fakes starve on the cost of entry.
